text:
The change sets MTU to 9000 on one SEA interface (10.0.3.5/30, OSPF area 0, cost 10). The neighbor on that link is not named in the ticket, so the tests below avoid assuming a specific peer and check invariants instead: no reachability or route regressions, and that a 1500-byte DF probe still passes through the changed interface. Because only one side of the link may be 9000, an MTU mismatch could break OSPF adjacency. I therefore include SEA adjacency checks to its likely neighbors (PAO, SDG, SLC) as "unchanged".

```json
{"tests": [
{"t":"adj","a":"SEA","b":"PAO","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"adj","a":"SEA","b":"SDG","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"adj","a":"SEA","b":"SLC","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"route","dev":"SEA","prefix":"172.16.1.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"route","dev":"SEA","prefix":"172.16.2.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"route","dev":"SEA","prefix":"172.16.3.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"route","dev":"SEA","prefix":"10.99.0.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"route","dev":"SEA","prefix":"10.98.0.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"c1-host","dst":"ext-dns1","svc":"udp/53","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"c2-host","dst":"ext-dns2","svc":"udp/53","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"c3-host","dst":"ext-dns1","svc":"tcp/443","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"c1-host","dst":"c2-host","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"c2-host","dst":"c3-host","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"c1-host","dst":"c3-host","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"noc1","dst":"c1-host","svc":"tcp/22","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"noc2","dst":"c3-host","svc":"icmp","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"noclab1","dst":"noc1","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"c1-host","dst":"noc1","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"reach","src":"ext-dns1","dst":"c1-host","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
{"t":"mtu","src":"c1-host","dst":"ext-dns1","size":1500,"expect":"pass"},
{"t":"mtu","src":"c3-host","dst":"ext-dns2","size":1500,"expect":"pass"},
{"t":"mtu","src":"c2-host","dst":"noc1","size":1500,"expect":"pass"},
{"t":"mtu","src":"c1-host","dst":"c3-host","size":9000,"expect":"fail"},
{"t":"mtu","src":"noc1","dst":"ext-dns1","size":9000,"expect":"fail"},
{"t":"conv","a":"SEA","b":"PAO","max_s":3},
{"t":"conv","a":"SEA","b":"SLC","max_s":3},
{"t":"load","a":"SEA","b":"PAO","max_pct":90},
{"t":"load","a":"SEA","b":"SLC","max_pct":90}
]}
```

Rationale for the MTU tests: hosts stay at 1500, so 9000-byte DF probes from hosts should still fail (the host-side interface limits them), confirming that no unintended end-to-end jumbo path was created. 1500-byte probes must continue to pass through the changed interface.
